fred-us-cpi-2026-08-12.standing: The monthly consumer price index from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the headline measure of what American households pay for goods and services. It sets the reference point for Federal Reserve policy and reprices bonds, currencies and rate expectations worldwide.
fred-us-cpi-2026-08-12.recent: The Fed held rates at 350-375 basis points on 29 July, citing elevated inflation, and the dollar has since fallen to its weakest since May. Fuel is the live channel: US diesel costs $5.36 a gallon, feeding through to food prices. This release is the first hard read on whether that war premium has reached the consumer basket.

fred-us-ppi-2026-08-13.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' producer price index, released monthly, measures what US producers receive for their output. It is read as an early signal of cost pressure moving through supply chains toward consumer prices.
fred-us-ppi-2026-08-13.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports US PPI on 13 August. The release will set the month's reading on producer-level cost pressure ahead of consumer prices.

fred-us-retail-sales-2026-08-14.standing: The Census Bureau's monthly estimate of receipts at US retail and food-service businesses, released about two weeks after the month it covers. It is the earliest broad read on consumer spending, which drives most of US economic output.

ecb-2026-09.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets interest rates for the euro area on a roughly six-week schedule. Its decisions set the cost of credit across twenty member economies and anchor the euro against every currency it trades against.

fomc-2026-09.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions move the cost of borrowing across the dollar economy and every asset priced against it.
fomc-2026-09.recent: The Fed held at 350-375 basis points in July, citing elevated inflation, after investors had priced a hike. Since then the dollar has fallen to its weakest since May, and Trump has renewed his bid to remove Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence. This meeting settles whether the fuel-led inflation of the summer changes the rate.

boe-2026-09.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who meet eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions set the floor for UK mortgage, business and government borrowing costs, and move sterling against the dollar and euro.
boe-2026-09.recent: At its July 30 meeting the committee held Bank Rate at 3.75%, with three of nine voting to raise and the Bank saying it was waiting to see the impact of the Iran war. UK house prices rose 0.1% in July as buyers stayed cautious on rates. September's vote will show whether that hawkish minority has grown.

boj-2026-09.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions set the price of the world's cheapest major funding currency, which makes them felt in the yen and in borrowing far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-09.recent: The Bank of Japan held at 1% on July 31 while warning underlying inflation is running above its 2% target, and Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours before that decision. Washington then joined a historic intervention on August 3, pushing the dollar to a one-month low. This meeting is the first test of whether the rate itself moves.

uk-cpi-2026-10.standing: The Office for National Statistics' monthly measure of UK consumer prices, released mid-month for the preceding month. It sets the reference point for Bank of England rate decisions, index-linked gilts, and a range of benefits and contracts uprated by inflation.
uk-cpi-2026-10.recent: The Office for National Statistics reports September consumer price inflation on 21 October. The release will settle where UK price growth stands going into the Bank of England's autumn decisions.

fomc-2026-10.standing: The rate-setting committee of the US Federal Reserve, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions set the price of dollar credit worldwide, moving currencies, sovereign borrowing costs and every asset priced in dollars.
fomc-2026-10.recent: The Fed held at 350-375 basis points in July, citing elevated inflation, after investors had priced a hike and Citadel bet on one. Since then the dollar has fallen to its weakest since May with a hike in doubt, and Trump has moved again to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence.

ecb-2026-10.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which sets the policy rates for the euro area's twenty-plus member economies at roughly six-week intervals. Its decisions transmit to borrowing costs across the bloc and to the euro's exchange rate.

boj-2026-10.standing: Japan's central bank, whose policy board meets eight times a year to set the short-term policy rate. Its decisions set the price of the world's cheapest major funding currency, transmitting to the yen and to carry trades built on borrowing it.
boj-2026-10.recent: The Bank of Japan held at 1% on July 31 while warning underlying inflation is exceeding its 2% target, and Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours before that decision. The US then joined a historic joint intervention on August 3, pushing the dollar to a one-month low. This meeting is the first policy setting since that coordination.

boe-2026-11.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who meet eight times a year to set Bank Rate. Its decisions set the floor for UK mortgage, business and government borrowing costs, and move sterling against every major currency.
boe-2026-11.recent: The committee held at 3.75% on 30 July with three of nine voting to raise, a split driven by the supply shock from the Iran war. UK house prices rose 0.1% in July as buyers stayed cautious on rates. This meeting settles whether the dissenting minority has grown.

fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the target range for overnight bank lending. Its decisions set the cost of borrowing across the dollar economy and reprice every asset quoted against the dollar.
fomc-2026-12.recent: The Fed held at 350-375 basis points in July, citing elevated inflation, and the dollar has since fallen to its weakest since May as a rate hike came into doubt. Trump has moved again to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence, and the Bank of England held at 3.75% with three dissents.
